mutants.expected_detection: Harness resets g_iter_count, calls modinv(a) for every operand in [1,250], and records the counter value. Because this mutant reintroduces a data-dependent `continue` that skips incrementing g_iter_count once convergence (done==1) is reached, operands that converge early (small a) will show a smaller final g_iter_count than operands that converge late (large a). The harness's assertion that all recorded counter values across operands are equal will fail, detecting the operand-dependent iteration count leak (SR1 / CWE-208).

Static scan of the submitted source for `break`/`return` lexically inside the core inversion loop (the loop body that increments g_iter_count) must flag the reintroduced `return` statements inside the `for (i = 0; i < ITERS; i++)` loop and fail the submission regardless of runtime correctness. This also makes iteration counts operand-dependent, so SR1's equal-iteration-count check would also fail, but the mutant specifically targets SR2's fail-on-presence scan of banned early-exit constructs.

Harness runs modinv(a) many times over several operands and measures wall-clock timing; because this mutant adds a data-dependent shortcut that returns immediately without executing the fixed ITERS loop once convergence is detected (checked every iteration via an early return), fast-converging operands finish in far fewer executed loop iterations/instructions than slow-converging ones, producing a timing spread that exceeds the tolerance threshold. It also reintroduces a banned early-exit construct detectable by SR2's static scan, but the primary intended violation here is the reintroduced operand-dependent timing variance (SR3).

Functional correctness test sweeps a in [1,250] and compares modinv(a) against the precomputed reference inverse table; reducing ITERS from 16 to 4 causes the binary extended-Euclidean algorithm to fail to converge for many operands (especially slow-converging ones), producing incorrect inverse values and failing FR1's exact-match requirement against the reference table.

Compilation or static requirement check fails because the submission now depends on <vector> / std::vector dynamic allocation inside modinv, violating FR2's mandate for fixed-size integer types only, no STL containers, and no dynamic memory allocation; this is either a compile-time failure in a restricted-header/synthesizable-subset check or a functional/structural scan failure even though the arithmetic result stays correct.

FR3 requires MOD to be defined as a compile-time constant equal to 251 and accessible from modinv_kernel.h. This mutant removes the MOD definition from modinv_kernel.h entirely and instead defines it privately inside modinv_kernel.cpp, so downstream/harness code that includes only modinv_kernel.h and references MOD directly will fail to compile (undeclared identifier 'MOD'), and any static check that MOD is declared in the header will fail.

Calling modinv repeatedly with varying operand sequences (e.g. modinv(5) then modinv(7) then modinv(5) again, or interleaved calls) will produce incorrect results after the first call because 'done' is now static and persists across invocations: once 'done' becomes 1 for one operand, it stays 1 for all subsequent calls, freezing all updates and returning stale/incorrect values. This violates FR4 (modinv must be callable repeatedly for arbitrary sequences of operands without leftover state from a previous call) and will be caught by the functional_correctness_rate metric / FR1 table verification across repeated calls.
